Based on the provided healthcare Q&A matches, it is not strictly necessary to insert a nasobiliary drainage (ENBD) tube routinely after endoscopic clearance of the common bile duct in patients with choledocholithiasis-induced cholangitis. While some healthcare providers may recommend its routine insertion, others have found that this approach does not improve the clinical course and can be associated with increased procedure time and discomfort.

In fact, a study suggests that inserting an ENBD tube did not improve the clinical outcome in patients who underwent endoscopic clearance of the common bile duct, despite the potential benefits for symptom relief. Therefore, healthcare providers may want to consider alternative management strategies, such as observation or less invasive interventions, before routinely inserting ENBD tubes.

It is essential to note that individual patient circumstances and treatment goals should be taken into account when making decisions about the management of choledocholithiasis-induced cholangitis. A thorough discussion with a healthcare provider can help determine the most effective approach for each patient.
